name: i-a-gun-time-from-race-timer
working: Two fleets, in the order defined: Lasers (event 1), then 420s (event 2).
race-timer's gun (event 5) fired at 12:02:00.000 by its at_ms, and reached the PRO's phone at 12:02:00.180, its device_ts. It landed on Lasers, the wrong fleet.
At 12:08:00 the PRO moved it to the 420s: event 7 undoes event 5, and event 8 is its copy on the 420s. The copy's device_ts is 12:08:00, when the fix was made, and its at_ms is still 12:02:00.000.
Lasers: its only gun, event 5, is undone, so it has no race and reads the race of the day. No rounding names Lasers, so its order is empty.
Lasers: mark_1 is stationed today (event 3, the mark phone's latest station pick, not undone; its role picks are not in the log) and holds no Lasers rounding, so it is waiting.
420s: its latest gun not undone is event 8, today. Its time is its at_ms, 12:02:00.000: no time fix names it. Not its device_ts, 12:08:00.
420s: event 4 names no race and was tapped at 12:01:30, before 12:02:00, so it is out. Event 6 names none and was tapped at 12:05:00, after 12:02:00, so it is in. Event 9, at 12:10:00, is in.
An implementation that reads the copy's device_ts would put the gun at 12:08:00 and leave event 6 out. That is what this vector catches.

420s: 51 (seq 3) and 9 (seq 4), each with 1 rounding, on one phone, so in the order that phone logged them. mark_1 holds both, so the 420s are not waiting for it. No rounding names no fleet, so there is no third order.
